info.name: RallyHub API
info.description:
RallyHub API (apps/api, NestJS). Generated from the controllers, DTOs, services and *.http.spec.ts suites on branch chore/api-dev-tooling.

## Setup
- Use the Postman desktop app (or the web app with the Desktop Agent) so the cookie jar works. Auth is cookie-based: Better Auth sets the session cookie and Postman sends it back automatically. Its name is `better-auth.session_token` over http (Local) and `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` when the API is served over https (e.g. a deployed Dev API), so look for that name in Postman's cookie manager. Cookies for the API host (e.g. `localhost`) must be allowed: in Postman open Cookies (under the Send button) and make sure the API domain is not blocked; if you use pm.cookies in scripts, add the domain to the allowlist there too.
- Pick an environment: **RallyHub Local** (API on http://localhost:3001, web origin http://localhost:3000) or **RallyHub Dev** (fill in every REPLACE_ME value).
- Credentials: both environments ship with empty `userPassword` and `secondPassword`. Set your own (8+ characters) before signing up; never commit them. In RallyHub Dev also replace `ownerEmail` / `secondEmail` with addresses only you use: the Dev database is shared, so a fixed address would collide with (or sign you in as) another developer. The Auth requests stop with a clear error while any of these are empty or still REPLACE_ME.
- API port: the API listens on `PORT` from apps/api/.env, which is 3001 in apps/api/.env.example; Docker Compose also publishes the API on host port 3001. If `PORT` is unset, apps/api/src/main.ts falls back to 3000, which collides with the web app (requests would reach Next.js), so keep `PORT=3001` or change `baseUrl` to match.
- Better Auth calls send `Origin: {{webOrigin}}`; the API must list that origin in BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS.
- Routes: Tenant, Tenant members, Court booking and Open play are URI-versioned (`/v1/...`). Health, Users, Venues and Courts are not versioned. There is no global prefix. Every route needs a session unless its description says Public.
- Context headers: `X-Tenant-Id: {{tenantId}}` (tenant members, venue create) and `X-Venue-Id: {{venueId}}` (court list/create, booking). Unknown ids are ignored, which gives 400 "... context required".
- Chained ids: requests that put an id in the path or a context header stop in their pre-request script when that id is empty (for example, Open play > Manage view with no `bookingId` would otherwise call `/v1/open-play/`, the public list, and return 200). Run the request named in the error first.
- Rate limits: sign-in and sign-up allow 5 attempts per 60 s per client IP (Better Auth, keyed on x-forwarded-for), then 429. Tenant create, status and delete share one budget of 5 requests per 60 s per signed-in user, then 429 for 60 s. Every other route allows 100 requests per 60 s per client IP and route, then 429 for 60 s. Limits are kept in memory per API instance.
- If the API runs with AUTH_DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL set, every request is treated as that user and the cookie is irrelevant; leave it unset to test permissions.

## Suggested run order
1. Auth > Sign up (owner) (or Sign in (owner) if the user exists). Saves `userId`.
2. In a terminal at the repo root: `npm run dev:make-admin -w api -- <your ownerEmail>` (`--revoke` undoes it). When the API's DATABASE_URL is not on localhost (e.g. the shared dev DB), the command refuses and names the host it found; re-run with `--remote=<that host>`. It refuses if `--remote` names a different host, so it cannot silently write to another database. Admin status is read from the database on each request, so no new sign-in is needed.
3. Users > Get current user (sanity check).
4. Tenant > Create tenant (saves `tenantId`), then Tenant > Update tenant status (ACTIVE).
5. Tenant members > Add member: adds you as tenant-wide OWNER. A platform admin can already manage everything else, but Open Play > Enable needs a real staff membership. (First-owner claim: a non-admin can add themselves as the first OWNER only when their email equals the tenant's email, is verified, and the tenant has no members yet; email/password sign-up is unverified, so locally the admin adds the first owner.)
6. Venues > Create venue (saves `venueId`, `venueSlug`), Venues > Update venue (status ACTIVE), Venues > Replace booking settings.
7. Courts > Create court (saves `courtId`).
8. Court booking > Create booking: a public Open Play game 3 days ahead at 18:00 Asia/Manila (saves `bookingId`, `openPlayJoinToken`, `bookingReferenceId`).
9. Open play > List public games, View game by join link, Manage view, Set visibility.
10. Auth > Sign up (second user) (this switches the session). Run the **Expected refusals > As the second user** requests to see the 403s: Create tenant, Update tenant details, Find tenant, List members, Update venue, Create court, Manage view. Then Open play > Join via public listing (201), Expected refusals > Join via link while already seated (409), Open play > Leave game (204), and Expected refusals > Cancel game as second user (403, not the booker).
11. Auth > Sign in (owner), then Open play > Cancel game (204).
12. Cleanup / destructive last, as the owner: Expected refusals > As the owner (cleanup) shows the 409s (Update / Remove member on the last owner, Delete court / Delete venue once bookings exist). For the success paths: Tenant members > Add member with `{ "email": "{{secondEmail}}", "role": "STAFF" }`, then Update member and Remove member; Courts > Create court again, then Delete court (204); Tenant > Delete tenant (soft) last (then Expected refusals > Delete tenant again gives 400).

## Tests and coverage
- Every request in the resource folders (Health to Open play) asserts its success status, and every route in apps/api/src/*/*.controller.ts appears there exactly once, plus 6 Better Auth requests.
- Expected refusals repeats 15 of those routes on purpose. Each copy asserts the refusal status the run order expects and saves no variables, so the refusal steps are green too. If a main request shows red, the call really did not succeed (often because the session or a chained id is not what the run order assumes).
- The Postman Runner runs requests top to bottom, which is grouped by resource, not the run order above. Follow the run order by hand, or run one folder at a time in the session it needs.

## Chaining variables (set by test scripts)
userId, secondUserId (sign up / sign in); tenantId (Create tenant); memberId (Add member); venueId, venueSlug (Create venue; `newVenueSlug` is the generated candidate); courtId (Create court); bookingId, openPlayJoinToken, bookingReferenceId, bookingStart (Create booking). privateBookingId is manual (see Enable Open Play).

**Who may call:** Public (`@AllowAnonymous()`).

**Success:** 200 `{ "status": "ok", "message": "Hello World!" }`.

**Common refusals:**

item.name: Auth
item.description: Better Auth endpoints (basePath `/api/auth`). Every request sends `Origin: {{webOrigin}}`. The session cookie (`better-auth.session_token` over http; `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` when the API is served over https, e.g. a deployed Dev API) is stored by Postman's cookie jar for the API host and sent on every later request. Only one session is held at a time per host: signing in as another user replaces it. The pre-request scripts stop with a clear error when the email/password variables are empty or still `REPLACE_ME`: set your own values in the environment first.

exec: // Guard: stop before sending when a variable this request needs is empty.
// An empty id in the path can hit a different route (e.g. /v1/open-play/ is
// the public list) and an empty context header gives an unhelpful 400.
['ownerEmail', 'set it in your Postman environment (an address/password of your own; never commit it)'],
['userPassword', 'set it in your Postman environment (an address/password of your own; never commit it)']
throw new Error(pair[0] + ' is not set: ' + pair[1] + '.');

header.description: Better Auth rejects auth calls whose Origin is not in BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS.

request.description:
**Who may call:** Public.

**Success:** 200 `{ token, user: { id, email, name, emailVerified: false, ... } }` and a session cookie (auto sign-in). Saves `userId`.

**Common refusals:**
- 422 when a user with that email already exists (use Sign in instead).
- 400 for an invalid email or a password shorter than 8 characters (the pre-request script stops earlier when `ownerEmail` / `userPassword` are not set).
- 403 when Origin is not in BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS (always checked). 403 `MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN` when Origin is missing and the request carries a cookie; with no cookie and no Origin, Better Auth skips the check and the request is handled normally (e.g. 401 for bad credentials).
- 429 after 5 attempts within 60 s from the same client IP (sign-in and sign-up are counted separately); wait a minute.

**Notes:**
- Email/password sign-up leaves `emailVerified` false (no verification is configured). Platform-admin status cannot be set here; extra fields such as `isPlatformAdmin` are ignored.
- Next: grant yourself platform admin with `npm run dev:make-admin -w api -- {{ownerEmail}}` (when DATABASE_URL points at a non-local host, add `--remote=<that host>`; the command prints the host it found and refuses if it does not match).

request.description:
**Who may call:** Signed-in user.

**Success:** 200 `{ success: true }`; the session cookie is cleared.

**Common refusals:**
- 403 when Origin is not trusted, or 403 `MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN` when it is missing (sign-out always carries the session cookie, so a missing Origin is enforced here).

**Who may call:** Any signed-in user.

**Success:** 200 with the caller's user record (internal flags such as `isPlatformAdmin` are not included).

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 "Authenticated user was not found" if the session's user row no longer exists.

**Notes:**
- Not versioned (`/users/me`, no `/v1`).

item.name: Tenant
item.description: URI-versioned: `/v1/tenant/...`. A new tenant starts as PENDING; bookings need the tenant, venue and court all ACTIVE.

request.description:
**Who may call:** Platform admin only (`assertPlatformAdmin`).

**Success:** 201 `{ success, message, statusCode, data: Tenant }` (note: the body's `statusCode` field is always 200 even when the HTTP status is 201). Saves `tenantId`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 403 for everyone who is not a platform admin (tenant owners and staff included). Spoofed body fields like `actorId` / `isPlatformAdmin` are stripped.
- 400 when `email` is not an email or `tenantName` / `phone` are missing.
- 429 after 5 tenant create, status or delete requests in total within 60 s by the same signed-in user, then blocked for 60 s.

**Notes:**
- Required: `email`, `tenantName`, `phone`. Optional: `tenantOwnerName`, `primaryColor`.
- The tenant `email` matters for the first-owner claim rule (see Tenant members > Add member).

exec: // Guard: stop before sending when a variable this request needs is empty.

throw new Error(pair[0] + ' is not set: ' + pair[1] + '.');

query.description: Optional. Only return the tenant if it has this status (PENDING | ACTIVE | SUSPENDED | INACTIVE); otherwise 404. Any other value gives 400 listing the allowed values.

request.description:
**Who may call:** A platform admin, or an active member of this tenant with any role (OWNER or STAFF), tenant-wide or scoped to one venue (`AuthorizationService.assertCanReadTenant`).

**Success:** 200 `{ success, message, statusCode, data: Tenant }`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 when `status` is not one of PENDING | ACTIVE | SUSPENDED | INACTIVE (the message lists the allowed values).
- 403 for everyone else, including a non-admin asking for an unknown id (the permission check runs first, so existence is not revealed).
- 404 "We couldn't find that tenant." for a platform admin asking for an unknown id, or when `status` is given and does not match.

**Notes:**
- The route is declared as `find/:id/` (trailing slash); Express's default non-strict routing serves it with or without the slash.

request.description:
**Who may call:** Platform admin only.

**Success:** 200 `{ success, message, statusCode, data: Tenant }` with the new status.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown tenant (checked before permissions, so any signed-in user sees 404 for a missing id).
- 403 for non-admins, owners included.
- 400 when `status` is not one of PENDING | ACTIVE | SUSPENDED | INACTIVE.
- 429 after 5 tenant create, status or delete requests in total within 60 s by the same signed-in user, then blocked for 60 s.

**Notes:**
- Set ACTIVE before booking: bookings and Open Play joins need tenant, venue and court all ACTIVE.

request.description:
**Who may call:** Platform admin, or an active tenant-wide OWNER of this tenant (`assertCanEditTenant`). STAFF cannot.

**Success:** 200 `{ success, message, statusCode, data: Tenant }`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown tenant (before permissions).
- 403 for anyone else, including staff, venue staff, inactive owners and owners of other tenants.
- 400 when `email` is not an email.

**Notes:**
- All fields optional (partial of Create tenant): `email`, `tenantName`, `phone`, `tenantOwnerName`, `primaryColor`.

request.description:
**Who may call:** Platform admin only.

**Success:** 200 `{ success, message, statusCode, data: Tenant }`; the tenant is not removed, its status becomes INACTIVE.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown tenant (before permissions).
- 403 for non-admins.
- 400 "This tenant is already inactive/deleted." when it is already INACTIVE.
- 429 after 5 tenant create, status or delete requests in total within 60 s by the same signed-in user, then blocked for 60 s.

**Notes:**
- Destructive for the rest of the run order: an INACTIVE tenant's courts are no longer bookable. Run last, or set the status back with Update tenant status.

item.name: Tenant members
item.description: URI-versioned: `/v1/tenant-member/...`. Every request needs tenant context: `X-Tenant-Id: {{tenantId}}` (an `X-Venue-Id` of a venue in the tenant also works). The tenant always comes from that header, never from the body. Missing or unknown tenant id → 400 "Tenant context required".

// An empty id in the path can hit a different route (e.g. /v1/open-play/ is

throw new Error(pair[0] + ' is not set: ' + pair[1] + '.');

header.description: Resolves tenant context (looked up in the DB; an unknown id is ignored and the route answers 400 "Tenant context required").

request.description:
**Who may call:** An active tenant-wide OWNER of this tenant, or a platform admin. Otherwise only the first-owner claim: role OWNER, no `venueId`, `email` equal to the caller's own email AND to the tenant's email, the caller's email verified, and the tenant has no member rows at all (`isValidFirstOwnerClaim`).

**Success:** 201 `{ message, content: TenantMember }` where TenantMember is `{ id, userId, tenantId, venueId, role, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt }`. Message is "Member added successfully!..." for a new row, or "Member is reactivated" when an inactive row in the same scope was reactivated. Saves `memberId`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 for missing/unknown tenant context, an invalid email, a role other than OWNER | STAFF, or a non-UUID `venueId` (checked first, by the DTO/context).
- 400 for OWNER with a `venueId` (owners are always tenant-wide) or a `venueId` from another tenant. Checked last, after the permission check (403), the user lookup (404) and the existing-row check (409), so an unknown email gives 404, not 400.
- 403 for callers who are neither owner nor admin and do not meet the first-owner claim.
- 404 when no user has that email (the user must sign up first; email match is exact, and Better Auth stores emails lowercased).
- 409 when the user already has an active row in the same scope, or "Lots of changes are being made..." when the tenant lock is busy.

**Notes:**
- As sent, this adds the signed-in owner as tenant-wide OWNER. A platform admin can do everything else without a membership, but Open Play > Enable Open Play only accepts venue staff (OWNER/STAFF memberships), so run this before that request.
- The first-owner claim needs `emailVerified: true`, which email/password sign-up does not set, so in local testing a platform admin adds the first owner.
- To try Update/Remove member, change the body to `{ "email": "{{secondEmail}}", "role": "STAFF" }` (optionally `"venueId": "{{venueId}}"`) and send again; `memberId` then points at that row. Updating/removing the only owner gives 409 (see Expected refusals).

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).

**Notes:**

item.name: Venues
item.description: Not versioned: `/venues/...`. All routes need a session (none are public). Booking settings live under `/venues/:id/booking-settings`.

exec: // Guard: stop before sending when a variable this request needs is empty.
// An empty id in the path can hit a different route (e.g. /v1/open-play/ is
// the public list) and an empty context header gives an unhelpful 400.
throw new Error(pair[0] + ' is not set: ' + pair[1] + '.');
// Venue slugs are globally unique: generate a fresh one per run. It goes in
// newVenueSlug; venueSlug is only replaced when the venue is created, so a
// refused attempt does not break Find venue by slug.

header.description: Resolves tenant context (looked up in the DB; an unknown id is ignored and the route answers 400 "Tenant context required").

request.description:
**Who may call:** Platform admin, or an active tenant-wide OWNER or STAFF of the tenant in `X-Tenant-Id` (`assertCanCreateVenue`). Venue-scoped staff cannot.

**Success:** 201 with a Venue `{ id, tenantId, name, slug, status, address, city, state, zipCode, country, timezone, phone, email, website, logo, coverImage, description, createdAt, updatedAt }`. New venues are PENDING. Saves `venueId` and `venueSlug`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 for missing/unknown tenant context, missing `name`/`slug`, an invalid IANA `timezone`, or an invalid slug (3-63 chars, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens, no leading/trailing or double hyphen, not reserved like `www`, `app`, `api`, `admin`, `dev`, `test`, `demo`...).

// Builds a slot-aligned start 3 days ahead at 18:00 venue-local time.
// Assumes the venue timezone is Asia/Manila (UTC+08:00, no DST), as set by
// "Venues > Create venue". 3 days keeps Leave seat / Cancel outside the 24 h
// Open Play cutoff. Override by setting bookingStart yourself and
const day = new Date(Date.UTC(local.getUTCFullYear(), local.getUTCMonth(), local.getUTCDate() + DAYS_AHEAD));

header.description: Resolves venue (and its tenant) context. An unknown id is ignored and the route answers 400 "Venue context required".

request.description:
**Who may call:** Any signed-in user (no membership needed). The booking is owned by the caller; a spoofed email in the body is ignored.

**Success:** 201 `{ statusCode: 201, message, bookingReferenceID, bookingId?, openPlayJoinToken? }`. `bookingId` and `openPlayJoinToken` are only returned for Open Play bookings. Saves `bookingReferenceId`, `bookingId`, `openPlayJoinToken`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 for missing/unknown venue context; a `date` that is not a complete ISO 8601 instant with an offset (`Z` or `+HH:MM`, e.g. `2026-11-10T18:00:00+08:00`; date-only or offset-less input is rejected); `rentDuration` outside 1-24; `openPlayCapacity` outside 1-64; Open Play options on a private booking; or a venue rule violation: start in the past, beyond `horizonDays`, duration outside the venue's min/max, not on a slot boundary, or outside opening hours (evaluated in the venue's timezone).
- 404 when `courtId` is not a court of the `X-Venue-Id` venue.
- 409 "This court isn't taking bookings right now." unless court, venue and tenant are all ACTIVE; 409 when the slot overlaps an existing booking; 409 "Lots of players are booking..." when the court lock is busy.

**Notes:**
- The pre-request script sets `bookingStart` to 18:00 Asia/Manila three days from now (inside the PUT booking-settings hours, outside the 24 h Open Play cutoff). Sending twice gives 409 for the same slot; change `START_HOUR` or `DAYS_AHEAD` in the script.
- As sent this is a public Open Play game for 4 (the booker takes the first seat). For a private booking send `"isOpenPlay": false` and drop `openPlayCapacity` / `isOpenPlayPublic`.
- A private booking's id is not in the response. To try Open Play > Enable Open Play, look up the CourtBooking row by `referenceId` = `{{bookingReferenceId}}` (e.g. with Prisma Studio) and put its id in `privateBookingId`.
